chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام about the junub and the menstruating woman: may they use dye? He said: “There is no harm.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ الصَّالِحَ: a title referring to the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.يَخْتَضِبَانِ: the two of them apply dye

ai.seo_question: Can a junub person or a menstruating woman apply dye according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that there is no objection to a person in janabah or a menstruating woman using dye. It pertains to rulings of ritual purity and clarifies permissibility in a practical matter during states of major ritual impurity.
